approach: A five-arm symmetric fee bandit. Each afterSwap call reconstructs an implied fair price from post-trade spot and the active fee, updates a gated fair-price estimate, scores the trade by signed edge in Y units, and updates that arm's short-memory mean. Every arm is sampled once; later choices are greedy except for deterministic epsilon exploration at 1/16.
next: Use separate bid and ask arm estimates so the bandit can exploit the different adverse-selection and retail-flow conditions on each side.
Test a contextual or UCB policy with time-gap and trade-size features, including an explicit cost for high-fee intervals with no retail fills.
Compare the fixed 1/32 reward memory and 1/16 exploration rate against slower decay and lower exploration on paired tuning seeds.

convergence.definition: converged when one step-end fee accounts for at least 80% of the last 1000 step-end quotes
